newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland buys back $1.69 bln of its Brady bonds.
newsitem.headline: Poland buys back $1.69 bln of its Brady bonds.

text.p: Poland bought back $1.69 billion worth of its Brady bonds maturing October 27, 2024, reducing the outstanding amount of the bonds maturing on that day to $6.05 billion, the finance ministry said in a statement.
It said the operation reduced Poland's total foreign debt by more than four percent.

"To finance the purchase of the Brady bonds, the finance minister issued on May 7 and sold to the National Bank of Poland long-term bonds, denominated in dollars but serviced and redeemed in zlotys, which mature on October 27, 2024," the ministry's Wednesday statement said.
Poland's Brady bonds were issued as a part of a debt restructuring scheme agreed on with commercial creditors in 1994. Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
